title: Regional write affinity heuristics and controlled evacuation playbook for analytics ingestion
creator: Marisol Cheng
description:
Problem:
Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions require that usage analytics and event-level telemetry for their tenants remain resident in specified legal regions. Our current ingestion topology writes events to the nearest ingest endpoint but fan-out replication sometimes routes primary writes into non-compliant replicas during transient outages or planner-driven rebalancing. This creates residency drift and complicates auditability.

Goals:
- Ensure primary write affinity for tenant-scoped analytics to the tenant's designated region unless an explicit evacuation is triggered.
- Provide a deterministic, observable evacuation/playback mechanism when capacity or DR conditions require cross-region relocation.
- Maintain low tail latency for writes (<150ms p95) and preserve throughput targets for burst windows.
- Emit auditable markers and lineage so we can prove data residency guarantees for compliance reviews.

Constraints and non-goals:
- We will not change the on-disk replication format in this ticket. Changes should be limited to routing, metadata, and orchestration layers.
- This initiative must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployment modes; private deployments may opt-out of cross-region evacuation.

Proposal summary:
1) Affinity decision layer: introduce a lightweight affinity service that returns a region-coded write target for a tenant given current policy, recent health signals, and quota state. Responses are cached by ingest gateways for 30s with explicit TTL refresh.
2) Controlled evacuation state: when the control plane signals evacuation for a region or tenant, produce an evacuation token that includes timestamp, source-region, target-region, and an authoring trace id. Ingest gateways will attach the token to writes during the evacuation window.
3) Write tagging and lineage: every event written during normal writes or evacuation carries: tenant_id, write_region, authoritative_region, evacuation_token (if present), and sequence fingerprint. This metadata flows through the analytics pipeline and into materialized views for audit queries.
4) Read/replay gate: downstream replicas will accept cross-region writes only when the evacuation token is valid and the tenant policy allows. Otherwise, the ingest gateway must reject or queue writes depending on client SLA class.

Architecture notes and trade-offs:
- Heuristic TTLs vs aggressive propogation: short TTLs reduce stale routing but increase control plane load. We pick 30s as a compromise to favor routing correctness during bursts.
- Synchronous write fencing vs eventual acceptance: synchronous fencing would prevent any non-authoritative writes but increases p99 latency and amplifies availability coupling. We prefer a permissive model with explicit markers so audits can filter and we can implement compensating reconciliation if needed.
- Evacuation by policy vs operator-driven: support both automated evacuation triggers (regional health) and manual playbook invocation. Automated triggers will be conservative and require multiple signals (capacitypressure AND region-loss-detection).

Detailed rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging, 2 weeks): deploy affinity service in staging; add ingest gateway caching and tagging; add binary flag to set evacuation token behavior per tenant. Run ingestion traffic via blue/green to validate latency/throughput.
- Phase 2 (canary, 1 week): enable for low-risk tenants in us-west/eur-north for read-only audits of tags; run synthetic evacuation drills to validate downstream acceptance and replay gating.
- Phase 3 (gradual enablement, 2–4 weeks): opt-in for remaining tenants; monitor residency-sla and audit query surface; fix anomalies.
- Phase 4 (enforcement): flip enforcement for P0 tenants and publish residency reports to customers.

Observability & metrics to add:
- write_affinity_resolution.latency.p50/p95/p99
- writes_tagged_with_evacuations.count (broken down by tenant and region)
- cross_region_writes_rejected.count and accepted.count
- residency_drift.alert_rate (detected events where write_region != authoritative_region without evacuation token)
- audit_query_latency for residency verification reports

Testing and validation:
- Evacuation drill harness (unit + integration): simulate regional outage and verify token issuance, routing change, and downstream acceptance.
- Chaos tests: transient control plane partition where affinity service returns stale routing; ensure TTL behavior and reconciliation logic behave as expected.
- Privacy/compliance tests: produce residency report for sample tenant and validate auditability via lineage markers.

Rollback strategy:
- Control-plane toggle to disable affinity enforcement and revert to current nearest-write behavior.
- Replay utility to re-route misrouted events to authoritative replicas and annotate backfilled segments for auditors.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: increased control-plane load due to TTL refreshes. Mitigation: local caching, bulk refresh API for gateway pools, and soft-fallback to nearest region on hit storms.
- Risk: downstream systems may not have schema fields for evacuation token. Mitigation: backward-compatible optional fields and a schema migration window.
- Risk: operator error causing mass evacuations. Mitigation: multi-sig / approval flow in console for manual evacuations plus dry-run mode.

Open questions:
- Should evacuation tokens be signed (HMAC) to prevent forged tokens by compromised gateways? (security favours yes; impacts key management).
- For Private deployments, do we allow automatic cross-region fallback at all, or mandate manual approval?
- What retention window for lineage metadata is required for audit needs (90 days vs 365 days)?

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atl/confluence/analytics/regional-write-affinity-design (draft)
- Ingest gateway PR with tagging prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-gateway/pull/1842
- Evacuation playbook draft (internal runbook): https://drive.google.com/evacuation-playbook-draft
steps: Implement affinity service API and basic TTL cache at ingest gateway
Add write metadata tagging (tenant_id, write_region, authoritative_region, evacuation_token, seq_fingerprint)
Implement evacuation token generator and storage in control plane
Add downstream gating logic to analytics consumers to validate tokens
Run staging canary and evacuation drills
Enable metrics, dashboards, and residency report export
comments: 2025-02-12: Initial proposal posted. Reviewed with infra and compliance. Compliance requested explicit signed tokens for auditability.
2025-02-18: Spike completed for affinity service. Prototype resolves in ~12ms median, 60ms p95 under load. Derek to optimize cache layer.
2025-02-24: Design review notes: Add multi-sig for manual evacuations; make evacuation_token HMAC-signed. Added to spec.
2025-03-01: Gateway tagging PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-gateway/pull/1842. Integration tests failing on schema migrations — engineering to add optional fields fallback.
2025-03-05: Canary day 1: enabled for 10 tenants in us-west. Observed 0.3% of writes tagged for evacuation during synthetic drill (expected). No latency regression beyond 10ms p95.
2025-03-05: Next actions: finalize token signing approach, run extended chaos tests, and prepare customer communication for opt-in phase.
